name: Brambleheart
equipment: Wooden shield carved with flowering vines
A staff of living wood (druidic focus, sprouts leaves in spring)
A scroll case of pressed Feywild flowers
A seed pouch containing seeds from 30 different plants
A crystal vial of pure spring water from a fey crossing
A moss-covered blanket that smells of pine
features: Firbolg Magic (Detect Magic and Disguise Self 1/short rest each, appear up to 3 ft. shorter with Disguise Self)
Hidden Step (bonus action to turn invisible until start of next turn or until attacking/forcing a save, 1/short rest)
Powerful Build (count as one size larger for carrying capacity and push/drag/lift)
Speech of Beast and Leaf (can communicate simple ideas to beasts and plants, advantage on CHA checks to influence them)
Wild Shape (2/short rest, up to CR 1 beasts, no swimming forms yet; lasts up to 2.5 hours)
Balm of the Summer Court (pool of d6s equal to druid level — 5d6; as bonus action, spend dice to heal a creature within 120 ft., target also gains temp HP equal to dice spent; restores on long rest)
Hearth of Moonlight and Shadow (during a short or long rest, create a 30-ft. sphere of dim light that grants +5 to Stealth and Perception checks for allies resting within)
Discovery (Hermit feature — discovered a unique truth about the connection between the Feywild and Wonderland)

personality.traits: I speak softly, rarely say more than necessary, and listen to the earth and plants for guidance. I hum quietly when I work, an old Firbolg tune that seems to soothe animals and make plants grow faster. I find beauty in everything natural — and Wonderland's twisted nature both fascinates and grieves me.
personality.ideals: Harmony. All living things are connected in the great web of nature. When one part sickens, all parts suffer. Wonderland's corruption is spreading through the fey crossings into the natural world, and it must be healed at the source.
personality.bonds: My grove sits at a fey crossing that connects to Wonderland. For years I protected it, but the corruption seeping through has begun to kill the ancient trees. I came through to heal the sickness at its root. I carry seeds from my grove — if I can plant them in Wonderland's soil, they may help restore the realm's natural balance.
personality.flaws: I am deeply uncomfortable in unnatural environments and Wonderland is the most unnatural place I have ever encountered. Talking flowers, inverted gravity, and sentient furniture distress me in ways that combat never does. I also struggle with the concept that in Wonderland, nature's rules do not apply — mushrooms grant size changes, animals form governments, and trees hold opinions. This challenges everything I believe.

appearance: A towering firbolg standing 7'4" with bark-brown skin dappled with patches of soft green moss that grows naturally on their shoulders and forearms. Their eyes are deep amber, warm and patient, like sunlight filtered through autumn leaves. Long hair the color of wild grass hangs in loose braids woven with small flowers and leaves — some living, some pressed. Their face is broad and gentle, with high cheekbones and a wide, kind mouth that seems more accustomed to silence than speech. They wear hide armor crafted from ethically shed deer hide, decorated with carved wooden beads. A living-wood staff sprouts small leaves and the occasional flower, responding to Brambleheart's emotions. Their hands are enormous and gentle, stained green from decades of herbalism. They move with the slow, deliberate grace of a large creature that has learned to be careful around smaller, more fragile things.
backstory: Brambleheart has been the guardian of a fey crossing deep in the Thornweald Forest for over a century — a patient, solitary steward of the boundary between the material plane and the Feywild. The crossing manifested as a circle of ancient oaks whose roots reached into both worlds, and through it flowed a gentle exchange of fey energy that kept the forest vital and magical. Brambleheart lived in harmony with this crossing, tending it as a druid tends a garden, ensuring that neither world bled too much into the other. Five years ago, something changed. The energy flowing through the crossing turned sour. The ancient oaks began to wilt, their leaves curling into playing-card shapes before falling. The forest animals grew confused and anxious, some speaking in riddles before forgetting how to speak at all. Mushrooms sprouted overnight in impossible colors, and Brambleheart found one that made a squirrel grow to the size of a bear before shrinking to the size of a thimble. The corruption was unmistakable — something was wrong on the other side of the crossing. Brambleheart studied the crossing for years, trying to heal it from the material side, but the corruption's source was beyond reach. Through communion with the oldest trees — those whose roots touched Wonderland's soil — Brambleheart learned fragments of truth: a realm of creative chaos imprisoned under a tyrant's order, a shattered mirror, a land slowly dying. The druid made the difficult choice to leave their grove and cross over, carrying seeds from the healthiest trees — seeds infused with genuine natural magic that might help restore what had been broken. Wonderland is everything Brambleheart fears: nature twisted into impossible shapes, governed by whim rather than cycle. But beneath the madness, the druid can feel Wonderland's original heartbeat — a rhythm of joy and creation that has been muffled but not silenced. That heartbeat is worth saving.
